name: How much space do you need for a bathroom addition in a small Los Angeles home?

mainEntity.name: How small can a bathroom addition be while still meeting code and feeling usable?
mainEntity.text: How small can a bathroom addition be while still meeting code and feeling usable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The smallest workable bathroom addition depends on the type of bath and the existing structure. A half bath can fit in roughly 18 to 20 square feet if the layout is tight and plumbing access is close. A full bath usually starts around 35 to 40 square feet, but most homeowners are happier with 50 to 60 square feet because it gives better circulation, storage, and fixture spacing. In older Los Angeles homes, the challenge is often not just room size but how to route plumbing, ventilation, and electrical safely. A good design also considers door swing, shower clearance, and whether the room will feel cramped once a vanity and toilet are installed. If space is limited, a pocket door, wall-hung vanity, or curb-less shower can make the addition more functional without expanding the footprint.
acceptedAnswer.description: A compact half bath can work in about 18 to 20 square feet, while a full bath usually needs at least 35 to 40 square feet. A more comfortable layout is 50 to 60 square feet. Clearances around the toilet, vanity, and shower matter as much as total square footage.
